name: Starter: Arabic
about: Modern Standard Arabic word order, gender and its joined little words in real, everyday sentences, every word with its vowels until you know it.

words.ليس: isn't, aren't (لَيْسَ عِنْدِي: I don't have)
words.أخ: brother (إِخْوَة: brothers; siblings for a mixed group)
words.عند: at (عِنْدِي: I have; عِنْدَكَ: you have)
words.كوب: glass, cup (كُوبُ مَاءٍ: a glass of water)
words.سكن: to live, in a place (يَسْكُنُ: he lives)
words.ذهب: to go (أَذْهَبُ: I go; سَنَذْهَبُ: we'll go)
words.يوم: day (الْيَوْمَ: today; يَوْمَ السَّبْتِ: on Saturday)
words.حال: state, condition (كَيْفَ حَالُكَ: how are you)
words.بحث: to look (بَحَثَ عَنْ: to look for)
words.عن: about; from (بَحَثَ عَنْ: to look for)
words.وجب: to be necessary (يَجِبُ أَنْ: must, have to)
words.جزيل: plentiful (شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا: thank you very much)
words.ل: to, for (لِي: to me, for me)
words.حذاء: shoe; footwear (حِذَاءٌ جَدِيدٌ: a new pair of shoes)
words.انتظر: to wait, for (تَنْتَظِرُنَا: is waiting for us)
words.مع: with (مَعِي: with me; مَعَنَا: with us)
words.عطلة: time off (عُطْلَةُ نِهَايَةِ الْأُسْبُوعِ: the weekend)
words.اتصل: to call (اتَّصَلَ بِـ: to call someone)
words.منذ: since; for (مُنْذُ سَنَةٍ: for a year)
words.كان: was (كُنْتُ: I was; كَانَتْ: she, it was)

kayfa-haluka.about: Literally how is your state; to a woman, حَالُكِ.

min-fadlika.about: Literally from your kindness; to a woman, فَضْلِكِ.

shukran-jazilan.about: Literally plentiful thanks; the answer is عَفْوًا.

utlat-nihayat-alusbu.about: Literally the time off of the end of the week.

concept.line: A present-tense verb usually starts with a letter that helps show who does it: أَسْكُنُ (I live), تَسْكُنُ (you live or she lives), يَسْكُنُ (he lives), نَسْكُنُ (we live).
A sentence about something now needs no word for am, is or are: الْبَيْتُ كَبِيرٌ (the house is big); أَنَا طَالِبٌ (I'm a student).
A pronoun joins the end of a noun, a verb or a little word: كِتَابِي (my book), اسْمُكَ (your name), لِي (to me), مَعَنَا (with us), انْتَظِرْنِي (wait for me).

words.means: عندي = I have; عندك = you have
مفتاحي = my key; المفتاح = the key

concept.line: A yes/no question can start with هَلْ and keeps a statement's order (هَلْ تَتَكَلَّمُ الْإِنْجِلِيزِيَّةَ؟); in a direct question a word like مَاذَا, أَيْنَ, مَتَى, كَيْفَ or كَمْ comes first (أَيْنَ الْمَحَطَّةُ؟), and the same words can introduce an indirect question: لَا أَعْرِفُ أَيْنَ يَسْكُنُ.

words.means: تتكلم = you speak; أتكلم = I speak
أفهم = I understand; تفهم = you understand

concept.line: الْ joined to the front of a word means the, and Arabic has no word for a: بَيْت (a house), الْبَيْت (the house); it also marks things in general: أَشْرَبُ الْقَهْوَةَ (I drink coffee).

words.means: أسكن = I live; تسكن = you live; she lives
أذهب = I go; تذهب = you go; she goes

concept.line: Every noun is masculine or feminine (most feminine ones end in ـَة), and the words with it agree: بَيْتٌ كَبِيرٌ (a big house), سَيَّارَةٌ كَبِيرَةٌ (a big car).
